[[File:Tulisan_basa_sunda_buhun_buda.svg|nirbing|115x115px]] | familycolor = Austronesian | region = [[Sunda Kingdom]] | fam1 = [[Austronesian Languages|Austronesian]] | fam2 = [[Malayo-Polynesian languages|Malayo-Polynesian]] | script = [[Buda Script]]
[[Old Sundanese script]] | iso2 = | iso3 = osn | glotto = sund1255 | glottorefname = Old Sundanese | ietf = [https://www.iana.org/assignments/lang-subtags-templates/osn.txt osn] | image = P-044058.jpg | imagecaption = The inscriptions of ''[[Astana Gede inscriptions|Astana Gede]]'', records the old Sundanese language using [[Old Sundanese script]] | notice = IPA | era = 12th to 17th centuries; afterwards developed into the [[Sundanese Language|Sundanese]] towards the 18th century. }} '''Old Sundanese''' ([[Sundanese script]]: {{Sund|ᮘᮞ ᮞᮥᮔ᮪ᮓ ᮘᮥᮠᮥᮔ᮪}}, [[Old Sundanese script]]: [[File:Basa_Sunda_Buhun_Letters_in_Old_Sundanese_script.svg|nirbing|115x115px]], [[Buda script]]: [[File:Tulisan_basa_sunda_buhun_buda.svg|nirbing|115x115px]], [[Roman script]]: {{lang|su|Basa Sunda Buhun}}) is the earliest recorded stage of the [[Sundanese language]] which is spoken in the western part of Java, [[Indonesia]]. The evidence is recorded in inscriptions from around the 12th{{Cite web|date=28 August 2010|title=Prasasti Geger Hanjuang|trans-title=Geger Hanjuang Inscription|url=https://pustaka.unpad.ac.id/wp-content/uploads/2010/08/pikiranrakyat-20100828a-prasastigegerhanjuang.pdf|access-date=5 September 2021|website=pustaka.unpad.ac.id|language=id}} to 14th centuries and ancient [[palm-leaf manuscript]]s from the 15th to 17th centuries AD. Old Sundanese is no longer used today, but has developed into its descendant, [[Sundanese language|modern Sundanese]].{{Cite book|last=Iskandarwassid|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=2stkAAAAMAAJ&q=kamus+istilah+sastra+sunda|title=Kamus istilah sastra: pangdeudeul pengajaran sastra Sunda|date=1992|publisher=Geger Sunten|language=su}} == Written evidence == Old Sundanese is recorded in stone inscriptions such as the [[Astana Gede inscriptions|Kawali inscription]] in [[Ciamis Regency|Ciamis]], and the [[Batutulis inscription]] in [[Bogor]], as well as in inscriptions made from copper plates such as the [[Kabantenan inscription]] from the [[Bekasi Regency]].{{Cite book|last=Djafar|first=Hasan|url=https://onesearch.id/Record/IOS1.INLIS000000000098583|title=Prasasti-prasasti dari masa kerajaan-kerajaan Sunda / oleh Hasan Djafar|date=1991|publisher=[s.n.]}}{{Cite journal |last=Hasan Jafar |first=Titi Surti Nastiti |year=2016 |title=Prasasti-prasasti dari Masa Hindu Buddha (Abad ke-12-16 Masehi di Kabupaten Ciamis, Jawa Barat |journal=Purbawidya |volume=5 |issue=2 |pages=101–116}} Other remains documenting the use of Old Sundanese are [[palm-leaf manuscript]]s from the [[Bandung]], [[Garut]], and [[Bogor]] regions. The manuscripts are now stored in several institutions, including Kabuyutan Ciburuy in Bayongbong [[Garut]], [[Sri Baduga Museum]] in [[Bandung]], the [[National Library of Indonesia]] in [[Jakarta]], and the Bodleian Library in London.{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=Cvp6AAAACAAJ|title=Katalog induk naskah-naskah nusantara: Perpustakaan Nasional Republik Indonesia|date=1990|publisher=Djambatan|isbn=978-979-428-151-2|language=id}}{{Cite book|last=Ekajati|first=Edi Suhardi|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=RheSrkiK2zYC|title=Jawa Barat, koleksi lima lembaga|date=1999|publisher=Yayasan Obor Indonesia|isbn=978-979-461-331-3|language=id}}{{Cite book|last1=Chambert-Loir|first1=Henri|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=5A4_OlCkEZgC|title=Khazanah naskah: panduan koleksi naskah-naskah Indonesia sedunia|last2=Fathurahman|first2=Oman|date=1999|publisher=Yayasan Obor Indonesia|language=id}}{{Cite book|last=Ekajati|first=Edi Suhardi|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=xZy49RnZcpEC|title=Direktori naskah Nusantara|date=2000|publisher=Yayasan Obor Indonesia|isbn=978-979-461-334-4|language=id}} == Characteristics == === Lexicon === The vocabulary used in Old Sundanese is still mostly recognizable for speakers [[Sundanese language|modern Sundanese]], either with the same meaning or having undergone a change of meaning. The use of [[Sanskrit]] which is adapted to the pronunciation or writing of the ancient Sundanese is mixed quite clearly. This is because of the nuances of the use of ancient Sundanese in [[Hinduism|Hindu]] and [[Buddhism|Buddhist]] religious texts. In some parts, the same vocabulary is often found, even combined with sentence strings in [[Old Javanese]].{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=M6tkAAAAMAAJ|title=Three Old Sundanese Poems|date=2006|publisher=K.I.T.L.V.|first1=J|last1=Noorduyn|first2=A|last2=Teeuw|isbn=978-90-67-18182-2}} In other parts, we also find the use of [[Old Malay]]{{Cite book|date=2000|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=iGJkAAAAMAAJ&q=kamus+sunda+kuno|title=Kosakata Melayu dalam naskah Sunda kuno: deskripsi dan dampak homonimi|publisher=Pusat Pembinaan dan Pengembangan Bahasa, Departemen Pendidikan Nasional|isbn = 9789794590041|language=id}} vocabulary and [[Arabic]].{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=1lMLAQAAMAAJ&q=gambaran+kosmologi+sunda|title=Gambaran kosmologi Sunda, kropak 420: silsilah Prabu Siliwangi, Mantera Aji Cakra, mantera Darmapamulih, ajaran Islam, kropak 421, jatiraga, kropak 422|last=Darsa|first=Undang A.|date=2006|publisher=Kiblat Buku Utama|isbn=978-979-3631-77-6|language=id}} The lexicon of Old Sundanese has been collected in an Old Sundanese–Indonesian dictionary.{{Cite book|last1=Sumarlina|first1=Elis Suryani Nani|last2=Darsa|first2=Undang A.|date=2003|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=UKAMAQAAMAAJ|title=KBSKI: Kamus Bahasa Sunda Kuno Indonesia|publisher=Alqaprint Jatinangor|isbn=978-979-9462-42-8|language=id}} === Morphology === The morphology of word formation can generally be recognized in modern Sundanese with some exclusions, for example the use of the [[prefix]] a- in the word ''awurung''. The [[suffix]] -''keun'' has a grammatical function similar to that of -''kan'' in [[Indonesian language]]. In addition, the use of insertion affixes ([[infix]]) ''-in-'' and ''-um-'' in the word ''ginawé'' ([[word stem]] ''gawé;''' 'to do') and ''gumanti'' (the root word ''ganti:'' 'replace') are insertions that are classified as productive used in old Sundanese, now words that include ''-in-'' and ''- um-'' is often considered monomorphemic. The following words are often not perceived as interpolated words such as ''sumebar'' which consists of ''sebar'' and ''-um-'', ''cumeluk'' which consists of ''celuk'' and ''-um-'' or ''tinangtu'' which consists of ''tangtu'' and ''-in-'' and ''pinareng'' consists of ''pareng'' and ''-in-''.{{Cite book|last=Arifin|first=E. Zaenal|date=1996|url=https://labbineka.kemdikbud.go.id/bahasa/jendelabuku/f90f2aca5c640289d0a29417bcb63a37|title=Seluk Beluk Morfologi Bahasa Sunda|location=Jakarta|publisher=Pusat Pembinaan dan Pengembangan Bahasa|isbn=979-459-448-2|pages=14|oclc=777998266}} The last is the use of insertion ''-ar-'' which serves to make a noun or adjective plural, for example in the word ''karolot'' (word stem ''kolot;'' 'the elders') which is still used until now.{{Cite web |last=Nurwansah |first=Ilham |title=Afiksasi dalam Bahasa Sunda Kuno (Analisis morfologis terhadap teks abad ke-16) |url=https://www.academia.edu/12307269 |website=Academia |language=id}} === Syntax === At the syntactic level, in general the sentence form in ancient Sundanese still has similarities with modern Sundanese.{{Cite book|title=Kajian Diakronis Struktur Bahasa Sunda Bihari dan Bahasa Sunda Kiwari|last=Ruhaliah|date=1997|publisher=IKIP|isbn=|location=Bandung|pages=}}{{Cite journal|last1=Nurwansah|first1=Illam|last2=Sudaryat|first2=Yayat|last3=Ruhaliah|first3=Ruhaliah|date=2017|title=SUNDANESE SENTENCE IN THE 16TH CENTURY ANCIENT SUNDANESE PROSE TEXT (Structure and Semantic Analysis)|url=https://ejournal.upi.edu/index.php/lokabasa/article/view/14199|journal=Lokabasa|language=en-US|volume=8|issue=2|pages=181–196|doi=10.17509/jlb.v8i2.14199|issn=2528-5904|doi-access=free}} One of the features of ancient Sundanese that can be distinguished from the structure of modern Sundanese is the use of the predicate-subject pattern in the sentence structure of the ancient Sundanese language with predicates in the form of a verb (verb) and a subject in the form of a noun (noun) which is quite consistent. Another characteristic feature is the use of ma particles which can act as reinforcement for previous phrases or clauses. In sentence construction, the particle ma functions as a marker that separates the clauses, and serves to introduce new information.{{Cite web|url=http://kbi.kemdikbud.go.id/kbi_back/file/dokumen_makalah/dokumen_makalah_1540522016.pdf|title=Function and Position of Particle ma in Old Sundanese|last1=Gunawan|first1=Aditia|last2=Fauziyah|first2=Evi Fuji|date=2018|website=kbi.kemdikbud.go.id|language=en|access-date=18 June 2020|archive-date=17 July 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220717163107/http://kbi.kemdikbud.go.id/kbi_back/file/dokumen_makalah/dokumen_makalah_1540522016.pdf|url-status=dead}} == Writing system == {{Main|Old Sundanese script|Buda script}} [[File:Kawali Sundanese script gap up.svg|thumb|Kawali [[Old Sundanese script]]]] [[File:Old sundanese script.svg|thumb|Carita Ratu Pakuan [[Old Sundanese script]]]] [[File:The Letters in Buda Script.svg|thumb|[[Buda script]]]] Writing systems that use the Old Sundanese language include [[Old Sundanese script]] and [[Buda script]]. These two characters can be seen from the inscriptions and ancient manuscripts stored in a place called Kabuyutan.{{Cite web|date=2021|title=Retrieving heritage: rare old Javanese and old Sundanese manuscripts from West Java (stage one) (EAP280)|url=https://eap.bl.uk/project/EAP280|access-date=20 October 2021}} These two characters has different functions. Old Sundanese script usually can be found on the inscriptions describing important events that occurred in the [[Sunda Kingdom|Sundanese region]], while the Buda script is widely used to write things that have a high level of sacredness in lontar or gebang manuscripts.Nurwansah, Ilham. Date accessed: 20 October 2021. doi: https://doi.org/10.33656/manuskripta.v7i1.81. == Example usages == [[File:KITLV 87606 - Isidore van Kinsbergen - Inscribed stone at Kawali near Tjiamis - Before 1900.tif|thumb|[[Astana Gede inscriptions|Kawali I inscription]] in ''kabuyutan'' area of Astana Gede, Kawali.]] === Inscription === The following is an example of the use of the old Sundanese language recorded in the Kawali inscription. Diplomatic transliteration was done by archaeologists Hasan Jafar & Titi Surti Nastiti. ''"nihan tapak walar nu sang hyang mulia tapa(k) inya parĕbu raja wastu mangadĕg di kuta kawali nu mahayu na kadatuan surawisesa nu marigi sakuliling dayĕh najur sakala desa aya ma nu pa(n)deuri pakĕna gawe rahayu pakĕn hĕbĕl jaya dina buana"'' Translation: These are the traces (tapak) (in) Kawali (of) the hometown of His Majesty King Wastu (who) established the defense (reigned in) Kawali, who had beautified the Surawisesa palace, which made a defensive trench around the royal territory, which prospered the whole settlement. To those who are to come, should apply salvation as the foundation of victorious life in the world. === Old manuscripts === The old Sundanese language used in lontar and gebang manuscripts can be
